pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Acute Thallium Toxicity (Thallotoxicosis) THE SMOKING GUN: The triad of severe GI distress, painful axonal neuropathy (burning allodynia), and sudden diffuse hair loss (anagen effluvium) with dark melanin pigment rings at the hair root bases under microscopy. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Thallium ions closely mimic potassium ions (K+) in ionic radius and charge, allowing thallium to readily enter cells via potassium transport channels and intracellularly inhibit the Na+/K+-ATPase pump. It avidly binds to sulfhydryl groups on mitochondrial proteins and cofactors (disrupting pyruvate oxidation, the Krebs cycle, and oxidative phosphorylation). This selective metabolic disruption causes rapid, dying-back axonal degeneration of small and large nerve fibers, as well as an abrupt arrest of protein synthesis in the mitotic matrix of hair follicles, leading to classic anagen effluvium. Treatment involves administration of Prussian Blue (potassium ferric hexacyanoferrate), which traps thallium in the gastrointestinal tract via ion exchange to prevent enterohepatic recirculation.
